SIZE / REPORTED APPLICATION FIELDS

How does reported space relate to outcomes?

Descriptive comparisons of decided applications. Reported and derived areas are not a plan-based compliance assessment.

ASSOCIATION, NOT PREDICTION

Recorded refused share by area band

Percentages use permitted + rejected applications with a positive reported/derived area. Counts are displayed for every band. These bands are descriptive and do not define legal minimum sizes.

Extractor-flagged space shortfall

The supplied flag compares reported flat sizes against the lowest bedroom-count standard used by its extractor. Missing occupancy and partial size schedules limit this test. “No flagged shortfall” does not establish compliance.

A source storey value of three is available for 798 applications in this release. It can refer to existing or proposed buildings. It is not a verified filter for existing three-storey houses.
SECOND TRY / MATCHED SITES

What happened to the next application?

A refused conversion matched to a later conversion at the same site, within four years. These are algorithmic matches, not verified design-change effects.

MATCHED PAIRS

Global filters apply to the refused application, including its start year and outcome. Appeals and later householder/HMO applications are outside this table.

Outcome of the next matched application

Pair-based counts. One site can contribute several pairs; an approved next application does not establish construction or explain which change mattered.

Decision text supplied for the refused application

A later approval may concern a different scheme at the same site. Changes mentioned in descriptions can miss the important revisions in drawings. Parsed flat counts and change tags can be wrong.

METHOD / TWO SEPARATE RELEASES

Show the working.

Supplied conversion extract

6,396 text-screened applications. Start dates 1 January 2019–30 October 2026; 2026 is incomplete. Files were supplied on 7 November 2026; an exact query timestamp and query/classification scripts were not provided. All application IDs join to the supplied raw candidate file in the local audit. Source-field values and classifications are not document verification.

Supplied decision=approved maps to Permitted, refused to Rejected, withdrawn to Withdrawn, pending/unknown to Undecided and other to Other. Original decision wording is retained. Rates use permitted + rejected only.

Reasons, sizes and resubmissions

Refusal categories use rules on decision text, with 4,175 application/category rows for 1,283 of 2,584 refusals. Reasons can overlap. Evidence snippets are supplied excerpts. No category is inferred for missing text. Size fields are reported or derived; house area / parsed flat count is a proxy, not each flat’s actual area. Extractor space flags do not establish compliance. Matched resubmissions are descriptive associations; global filters apply to the refused side. All flat counts and change tags remain unverified, including a known P0826 count/description conflict.

Supplied refusal-classification method ↗
Supplied site-matching method ↗

Foundations keyword snapshot

243,926 source records, 27 columns, updated 5 October 2026. Description requires flat/self-contained plus conversion/convert/subdiv/sub-div. The 5,377 candidates have start dates 2021–2025 and include commercial/reverse conversions, amendments and conditions. The 2,005 house-wording records are a heuristic. Outcome normalisation has known discrepancies. This release remains separate from the supplied conversion extract.

Common limitations

Zero plan-verified three-storey conversions in either release. Sky Fragment has 20 level entries (including mezzanine and roof), but no confirmed existing/proposed phase, London planning link, daylight results or verified dwelling schedule. Verified-only filters remain hidden. Borough/map shares are suppressed below 20 permitted/rejected records. Decision intervals require both dates and a finite non-negative duration; they do not establish legal deadline breaches. Applications and permissions are not delivered homes. Missing values are never converted into zero outcomes.
